nodes.title: Finite fields, trace, and self-dual normal bases
nodes.statement: For every odd natural k, instantiate the characteristic-two field GaloisField 2 k of cardinality q=2^k and its prime-field trace, prove that a Fin k-indexed basis exists which is simultaneously normal and self-dual, and select such a basis for the mathematical QPBT definitions. Keep the paper's single uniform deterministic basis-and-multiplication-table algorithm as the separate K03A complexity contract.
nodes.encoding: Instantiate Mathlib's GaloisField 2 k directly and derive its Field, Fintype, DecidableEq, CharP, cardinality, finite-dimensional algebra, and trace. Prove simultaneous normality and trace self-duality before making a noncomputable mathematical choice. Index the Frobenius orbit by Fin k, corresponding to the paper's exponents j=0,...,k-1. The algorithmic selection, multiplication-table output, and cost proof belong to K03A and must be proved coherent with this representation.
nodes.boundary_hypotheses: Universe levels are explicit for reusable carrier APIs. The field instances and simultaneous-basis existence theorem are derived from k and q=2^k with Odd k; no caller supplies a field, basis, normality proof, self-duality proof, algorithm, or arbitrary witness package.

integrity.paper_assumptions: A positive odd integer k and the concrete extension F_(2^k)/F_2; for the computational clause, k is input to one uniform deterministic construction.
integrity.lean_assumptions: k : Nat and Odd k, with the GaloisField, algebra, trace, finiteness, and decidability data derived internally; no basis, construction, algorithm, or witness package is supplied by a caller.
integrity.paper_conclusion: A basis exists which is simultaneously normal and trace-self-dual; one deterministic algorithm uniformly outputs such a basis and compatible multiplication tables in poly(k) time.
integrity.lean_conclusion: F01 proves simultaneous existence and exposes a noncomputably selected concrete basis and trace. K03A separately retains the uniform algorithm, table, representation-coherence, and complexity theorem.

nodes.title: Individual-degree polynomials and indicator encoding
nodes.statement: Define individual-degree polynomials, evaluation at field points, the linear low-degree encoding of data indexed by Boolean points, and the indicator vector evaluated at an arbitrary field point; prove Boolean interpolation and injectivity.
nodes.encoding: BooleanPoint m = Fin m -> ZMod 2 indexes codeword coordinates; FieldPoint k m = Fin m -> GaloisField 2 k is the evaluation domain. indicatorPolynomial y is the source product of X_i or 1-X_i factors, indicatorVector x is indexed by Boolean y, and lowDegreeEncode is a linear map into MvPolynomial.restrictDegree with bound one.
nodes.boundary_hypotheses: Natural k,m and the concrete F01 field type only. No FieldData or chosen basis is required; interpolation, the evaluation formula, linearity, and injectivity are proved facts rather than structure fields or assumptions.

integrity.paper_assumptions: A Boolean coordinate y in {0,1}^m, a field evaluation point x in F_q^m, and data a indexed by Boolean points.
integrity.lean_assumptions: BooleanPoint m, FieldPoint k m, and the concrete GaloisField 2 k; no basis data.
integrity.paper_conclusion: The indicator product, low-degree evaluation formula, Boolean interpolation g_a(y)=a_y, and linearity.
integrity.lean_conclusion: The individually degree-one polynomial subtype, the same evaluation and interpolation equations, a linear-map encoding, and injectivity derived from interpolation.

nodes.title: Finite measurements and postprocessing
nodes.statement: Represent arbitrary finite POVMs, projective measurements, observables, brackets, and outcome postprocessing on finite coordinate Hilbert spaces.
nodes.encoding: Use MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement for arbitrary POVMs and define projectivity as a separate predicate. Keep this namespace qualified and do not open or inherit the incompatible LDT measurement hierarchy.
nodes.boundary_hypotheses: Declare universe uOutcome uCoord and require [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome] [Fintype Coord] [DecidableEq Coord]; the Hilbert scalar is Complex and no infinite-dimensional completion is hidden.

integrity.paper_assumptions: Finite POVM outcomes; projectivity for the binary observable; and an arbitrary outcome function for postprocessing.
integrity.lean_assumptions: Explicit Fintype/DecidableEq outcome and coordinate types on qualified MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement; the question type remains arbitrary until averaging; projectivity is a separate proof input only where the paper requires it.
integrity.paper_conclusion: Postprocessing is the exact fiber sum, including zero for an empty fiber, and a projective F_2-valued measurement gives the observable effect 0 minus effect 1 with unitary involution laws.
integrity.lean_conclusion: The qualified measurement postprocess and its effect equation are callable, and the certified binary observable exposes the same operator body and laws with the paper's sign order.

nodes.title: Finite strategies, local isometries, and distance values
nodes.statement: Define normalized finite bipartite pure strategies; Alice/Bob local lifts; transparent side-specific rectangular isometry conjugation; certified tensor isometry and state action; junk/ideal reindexing; and separate finite numeric values and exact NNReal bounds for raw-operator and POVM-family state-dependent distance.
nodes.encoding: Use EuclideanSpace Complex carriers and a PureStrategy field whose norm-one proof bundles probability normalization. Convert rectangular isometries by Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm, conjugate each side independently as V*A*V^adjoint, lift local operators by Matrix.kronecker, certify the tensor map as a LinearIsometry, and expose Matrix.reindexAlgEquiv plus the matching state reindexing. Finite distance values return Real; exact bound predicates take NNReal. Indexed Big-O, consistency, and laws are separate dependent nodes.
nodes.boundary_hypotheses: Declare all question, outcome, local, auxiliary, junk, and ideal universes explicitly and require Fintype/DecidableEq only where finite sums or matrices need them. The state is bundled with norm one. No coercion among EuclideanSpace, WithLp, matrices, or operators is implicit, and no finite <= delta predicate is identified with the paper's indexed O(delta) relation.

integrity.paper_assumptions: Finite-dimensional bipartite pure strategies, normalized states, finite POVM or raw-operator families, finite distributions, and local isometries where extraction is used.
integrity.lean_assumptions: Explicit finite/decidable coordinate and averaged index types, PMFs, Euclidean coordinate carriers, and factored target types; no asymptotic premise enters this finite layer.
integrity.paper_conclusion: The finite expressions underlying state-dependent distance, local tensor actions, and side-specific V*A*V^adjoint conjugation.
integrity.lean_conclusion: Separate exact Real values and NNReal bounds, certified local/tensor isometry adapters, and explicit state/operator reindexing with the same formulas.

nodes.title: Indexed asymptotic state, operator, measurement, and strategy distance
nodes.statement: Define [0,1]-valued Nat-indexed error profiles; the paper's global positive-index Big-O predicate; an auxiliary atTop predicate with a public one-way bridge from the paper predicate; and global distance relations for state, raw-operator, POVM, and strategy families. The strategy comparison helper consumes explicit joint-PMF marginals and a first/second state choice; the paper-facing strategy relation existentially chooses one branch.
nodes.encoding: ErrorProfile is Nat -> Set.Icc 0 1, while derived law scales may be arbitrary Nat -> Real. PaperBigO follows the explicit top-level convention: one C > 0 bounds norms at every 0 < n; Lean's index zero is unconstrained. IsBigOAtTop remains an auxiliary Asymptotics.IsBigO Filter.atTop relation, and PaperBigO.isBigOAtTop exposes only the valid global-to-eventual direction. PMF.map Prod.fst/Prod.snd supplies the question marginals. StrategyStateChoice indexes the two comparison-state branches; StrategyFamiliesBigOWithChoice fixes one branch for both player comparisons, and the paper-facing StrategyFamiliesBigO existentially chooses that shared branch.
nodes.boundary_hypotheses: Finite question/outcome/coordinate types only at PMF sums, normalized states through PureStrategy, and explicit Nat-indexed data. Every paper-facing asymptotic relation uses one positive Real constant uniformly for all positive indices; no condition is imposed at zero. StrategyFamiliesBigO existentially chooses one shared state branch through StrategyFamiliesBigOWithChoice; the paper does not explicitly say whether Alice and Bob could choose different branches. No eventual bound is promoted back to a global bound, and no derived real scale is clamped to [0,1].

integrity.paper_assumptions: Positive-integer-indexed normalized states/strategies, delta : N -> [0,1], finite distributions, and state-dependent POVM/operator families; strategy distance permits either the first or second strategy state. The global preliminaries quantify one bound over every positive index, while the consistency footnote says n tends to infinity.
integrity.lean_assumptions: The same data over Lean Nat with 0 < n guards, explicit finite coordinate carriers, PMFs, and joint-PMF marginals; StrategyFamiliesBigOWithChoice takes one first/second comparison-state choice shared by the two player comparisons, and StrategyFamiliesBigO existentially quantifies it. IsBigOAtTop is auxiliary only.
integrity.paper_conclusion: Squared state norm and averaged operator/POVM distance satisfy the paper's global O(delta) convention, while strategy distance holds for an existential choice of either strategy state.
integrity.lean_conclusion: PaperBigO states the global positive-index component relations; PaperBigO.isBigOAtTop exposes their eventual consequence; and StrategyFamiliesBigO existentially chooses the shared StrategyStateChoice used by its helper.

nodes.title: Exact and asymptotic POVM consistency
nodes.statement: Define exact same-measurement consistency by equality of Alice/Bob local actions; define the finite off-diagonal mismatch value and exact bound; lift it to the paper's global positive-index Big-O consistency; and state the normalized-state three-premise global consistency-triangle contract with scale epsilon + 2*sqrt(delta+gamma).
nodes.encoding: The finite value is the PMF-weighted off-diagonal sum of real inner products after explicit Alice/Bob local lifts. MeasurementConsistentOn intentionally expresses the action equality for any POVM; the paper's exact-consistency definition additionally requires that M be projective. The paper-facing consistency relation and triangle conclusion use PaperBigO with one constant over every positive index; IsBigOAtTop is available only through the one-way bridge. The derived triangle scale is Nat -> Real and is not clamped back to [0,1]. The named Law declaration freezes the theorem statement, and its named theorem is proof-complete rather than a new assumption.
nodes.boundary_hypotheses: Finite question/outcome/local coordinate types and explicit indexed PMFs/states/families. Every paper-facing consistency bound is global over all 0 < n and imposes no condition at zero. The triangle Law and theorem take hpsi : forall n, norm (psi n) = 1 immediately after psi, then exactly the paper's three consistency premises. Paper uses of MeasurementConsistentOn must separately supply projectivity of M.

integrity.paper_assumptions: A projective measurement M for exact same-measurement consistency; positive-integer-indexed finite POVM families on a normalized bipartite state and distribution; for Proposition 4.29, the normalized state followed by the three displayed global consistency premises. The local n-to-infinity footnote conflicts with the explicit global Big-O convention.
integrity.lean_assumptions: MeasurementConsistentOn generalizes the action equality to an arbitrary finite POVM, with paper call sites separately requiring projectivity. The indexed triangle has explicit PMF and finite carriers, hpsi : forall n, norm (psi n) = 1, local tensor lifts, [0,1]-valued profiles, and PaperBigO premises quantified over every 0 < n; the derived scale is real-valued.
integrity.paper_conclusion: A projective M has equal Alice/Bob local actions exactly when consistent; off-diagonal outcomes satisfy the global O(delta) convention; and the three-premise consistency triangle has global scale epsilon + 2*sqrt(delta+gamma).
integrity.lean_conclusion: The reusable action-equality generalization, the same finite value, global positive-index consistency relation, and normalized-state global triangle Law/theorem with exact premise order and scale.

nodes.title: Finite two-player game and quantum strategy semantics
nodes.statement: Define finite two-player one-round games; a game-indexed wrapper around the established finite pure tensor strategy; exact strategy and supremal game values; projective, symmetric, support-commuting, consistent, PCC, and SPCC predicates; coefficient-matrix Schmidt rank; and the extended-natural entanglement requirement.
nodes.encoding: Reuse the accepted PureStrategy and MeasurementConsistentOn declarations. FiniteGame stores a PMF and Bool predicate. FiniteGameStrategy is a one-field game-indexed wrapper, not a second strategy representation. Quantify all finite Hilbert coordinates canonically by Fin dimensions, define game value by real sSup, Schmidt rank by Matrix.rank of the coefficient matrix, and Ent by WithTop Nat sInf so the empty attainable set is infinity.
nodes.boundary_hypotheses: Question, answer, and coordinate carriers are explicit finite decidable types. Shared-space predicates use one coordinate type for both players. Canonical Fin dimensions represent arbitrary finite coordinate Hilbert spaces. No executable sampler, machine description, cost model, caller-supplied semantic obligation, placeholder declaration, or public bridge assumption enters this node.

integrity.paper_assumptions: Finite question and answer alphabets, a question distribution, Boolean decision predicate, normalized finite-dimensional pure tensor strategies with POVMs, and a common local Hilbert space for commuting/consistent/PCC predicates.
integrity.lean_assumptions: Explicit Fintype/DecidableEq carriers, Mathlib PMF, the reviewed PureStrategy and MeasurementConsistentOn interfaces, and canonical Fin coordinate representatives for the dimension-varying extrema.
integrity.paper_conclusion: Exact fixed-strategy and game values; projective, symmetric, commuting, consistent, PCC, and SPCC predicates; Schmidt rank; and the minimum rank requirement or infinity.
integrity.lean_conclusion: The same formulas, predicates, supremum, matrix rank, and extended-natural minimum, with the game-strategy association represented by a data-free wrapper.

nodes.title: State-dependent distance triangle and consistency postprocessing laws
nodes.statement: Prove the finite squared-distance triangle bound with explicit factor 2, the global positive-index Big-O measurement triangle law where the constant is absorbed, and Fact 4.26 as global heterogeneous Alice/Bob POVM-consistency data processing under the same explicit outcome postprocess on both families.

The finite helper exposes factor 2 for squared norms; PaperBigO absorbs that universal factor while preserving one global constant over every positive index. Fact 4.26 is represented only by global POVMConsistencyBigO before and after applying the same MeasurementFamily.postprocess to heterogeneous Alice/Bob families; no same-space distance law retains that paper label. IsBigOAtTop is an auxiliary consequence, not a paper-facing conclusion.

Every paper-facing asymptotic premise and conclusion is global over all 0 < n with index zero unconstrained. Paper-labelled calls supply normalized states where the source's quantum-state convention requires them.

For Fact 4.26, heterogeneous Alice/Bob POVM families on a bipartite state, one global cross-player consistency relation, and one shared outcome map. The top-level global Big-O definition controls the local n-to-infinity ambiguity.

nodes.title: Generalized Pauli and Fourier algebra
nodes.statement: Define single- and multi-register generalized Pauli X/Z operators and projectors, their product laws and Fourier inversion, and the exact trace-valued twisted commutation phase; defer EPR and qudit-to-qubit conversion to F10.

Phases are ZMod.stdAddChar applied to fieldTrace, and Fourier inversion uses the explicit inverse field-cardinality normalization. F05 uses the integrated raw Op/Measurement API and not the unfinished BinaryObservable surface.

nodes.title: Conditionally-linear maps and samplers
nodes.statement: Define recursively certified conditionally-linear maps, their finite distributions, level raising, direct sums, and basis-mediated downsizing, together with mathematical conditionally-linear samplers.
nodes.encoding: The certificate is indexed by the current coordinate register, level, and realized function. Level zero certifies only the zero map; a successor partitions the register into disjoint complementary head/tail sets, applies a supported linear head map, and selects a recursively certified tail function by an element of the head-map range. Level raising repairs G20 internally by prepending an empty zero head and retaining the original function on the full recursive tail. Downsize repairs G21 internally by pulling prefixes back through the coordinate equivalence before conjugating each source map and by handling level zero with the existing zero certificate. Samplers map one uniform ambient vector to an explicit pair PMF. CLSampler.sample_directSum identifies the summed sampler with the independent product PMF after reindexing both left/right outputs by Fin.append.
nodes.boundary_hypotheses: All mathematical spaces and randomness in this node are finite. F01 FieldData is consumed only for mathematical downsizing and remains owned by F01. F06 ends at conditionally-linear.tex:552 and retains exactly its mathematical callables. F06A-EXECUTABLE-CL alone owns the binary-string representation, six-input dimension/marginal/linear/factor query machine with canonical blank normalization, associated sampler distribution and step count, valid-query finite maximum and global positive-index RuntimeBigO, executable downsizing transformation, dimension s(n) * log q(n), associated downsized maps, and O(TIME_S(n) log q(n)) runtime at conditionally-linear.tex:553-712. F07A-DETYPING, QPBT-043, K03, and K04 own none of that generic executable layer.

integrity.paper_assumptions: A finite coordinate field space and recursively selected complementary register subspaces; independent uniform coordinates across direct-sum factors; a selected basis only for downsizing.
integrity.lean_assumptions: Concrete characteristic-two field vectors, finite coordinate registers, and the recursive certificate; independent component PMFs combined by bind/map; F01 FieldData only at downsize.
integrity.paper_conclusion: The mathematical conditionally-linear functions and distributions through the downsize pushforward at conditionally-linear.tex:1-552.
integrity.lean_conclusion: The same mathematical operations, including an exact PMF equality after Fin.append reindexing and normalized downsize pushforward. F06A exclusively owns the subsequent generic executable sampler/query/downsize layer.

nodes.title: Executable conditionally-linear samplers
nodes.statement: Define an admissible positive-index field family and its canonical source-coherent binary field-vector codec. Define a genuine six-input Turing sampler with distinct dimension, marginal, linear, and factor query modes with canonical blank normalization of unused tapes, data-valued chosen CL decompositions with dependent valid prefix and factor domains, its associated maps and exact sampler PMF, and an exact operational maximum TIME_S(n) over valid queries plus intrinsic exponent computation. Define executable downsizing and prove field size 2, dimension s(n) * log q(n), associated downsized maps, exact PMF pushforward, and the global positive-index RuntimeBigO compiler-cost bound.
nodes.encoding: For every positive n, q(n) = 2^(exponent n) with Odd (exponent n), and Nat.log 2 (q(n)) is the paper's log q(n). The canonical field codec is the F01-selected basis/table representation, with fixed coordinate order; no caller-supplied codec or coherence premise is accepted. SixTapeInput is Fin 6 -> List Bool. CLSamplerQuery has exactly four constructors and its positive-index proof supplies the canonical codec to every query. Its canonicalTapes encoding exposes the paper layouts and writes [] on every unused tape; it does not assert invariance under arbitrary unused-tape contents. stage.val encodes paper j = stage.val + 1. packSixTapes first fixes tape order with List.ofFn and is an injective administrative encoding only. CLQueryDecomposition carries selected marginals, prefix-range-indexed factors, factor-space linear maps, and the lem:cl-kth realization equations, partition, support, and dependency laws as data. CLPrefix and CLFactorInput are the dependent valid u/y subtypes; malformed encodings and index zero are outside the paper contract. An intrinsic FieldExponentProgram computes exponent n from n; it is attached to the executable sampler and is not a fifth sampler query mode. The sampler PMF is exactly CLSampler.sample from one shared uniform seed.
nodes.boundary_hypotheses: The executable sampler is supplied as the source-defined machine together with intrinsic semantic correctness data; no theorem asserts that every mathematical CLSampler has an executable realization. Its associated maps and decomposition choices are data-valued and include the exact F06 lem:cl-kth laws. The machine has six logical input tapes with canonical blank normalization; the boundary does not claim the paper's stronger arbitrary unused-payload invariance. Its execution field contains a genuine TM2OutputsInTime witness and its exact step count is runInTime.toEvalsTo.steps. Any FinTM2 packing is injective administration and cannot replace the six-tape boundary. Every paper-labelled pointwise claim carries 0 < n, and downsizing carries 1 <= level. The paper does not specify how downsize computes log q(n); the faithful executable boundary therefore attaches a concrete FieldExponentProgram to the sampler rather than fabricating one from an arbitrary exponent family. TIME_S(n) is the exact maximum of that field-exponent execution and the valid-query finite maximum over Finset.univ; time is a definition, not an arbitrary upper-bound field. RuntimeBigO is global over positive indices. The source's omitted linear u/y quantifiers and the prefix/downsize index typos are preserved as explicit paper-gap notes A02-004/A02-006 and repaired only at the dependent Lean boundary. F01's source-coherent codec construction and table algorithm remain the tracked G16/K03A proof obligation, never a public codec-correctness input. The compiler-cost proof must account for parsing, prefix inversion, simulation, and ordered log-q factor-block output; it may not use a generic obligation. F06A alone owns def:sampler, def:sampler-sample, def:downsize_sampler, and lem:downsize_sampler. F06 owns only conditionally-linear.tex:1-552; F07A-DETYPING, QPBT-043, K03, and K04 own none of the generic executable sampler, query, distribution, downsize, dimension, or runtime clauses. No generic Hypotheses, Assumptions, bridge, residual, repair, witness, package, producer, arbitrary implication input, or fabricated Turing theorem is permitted.

integrity.paper_assumptions: Positive integers n with an admissible field size function q(n), a dimension function s(n), one ell-level six-input Turing sampler whose four query modes return chosen marginal maps, linear maps, and factor indicators for associated Alice/Bob CL functions, and ell >= 1 for executable downsizing.
integrity.lean_assumptions: An exponent family with Odd (exponent n) guarded by 0 < n, the canonical F01 source-coherent coordinate codec, an explicit Fin 6 binary query boundary with canonical blanks on unused tapes, data-valued nonunique CLQueryDecomposition records whose CLPrefix/CLFactorInput domains satisfy the F06 laws, an operational six-input machine, a concrete intrinsic FieldExponentProgram, genuine TM2OutputsInTime witnesses for both the four source queries and exponent computation, exact extracted execution steps, and a constructed operational maximum charging both kinds of execution; no executable-realization, codec-coherence, runtime, bridge, or arbitrary obligation premise is added to a paper theorem.
integrity.paper_conclusion: The sampler has associated CL maps, chosen decompositions, exact distribution, and TIME_S(n); its executable downsize has field size 2, dimension s(n) log q(n), associated downsized CL maps, exact sampler-law pushforward, and global positive-index runtime O(TIME_S(n) log q(n)).
integrity.lean_conclusion: The exact four encoded query results compute through six-tape operational run witnesses on canonical blank-normalized tapes and dependent valid-query domains; no arbitrary unused-payload invariance is claimed. Associated, sample, queryTime_eq_validQueryMax, and time_eq_max are callable; time_eq_max charges the intrinsic exponent program needed by downsize. Downsize has the canonical binary codec, an internal s(n)*exponent(n) representation width proved equal to dimension s(n)*Nat.log 2(Q.fieldSize n), exact pointwise map correspondence for every 0 < n, exact PMF.map pushforward from one shared sampler law, and a proved global-positive RuntimeBigO compiler-cost theorem under 1 <= level. The G16/K03A representation-coherence obligation remains tracked and is not exposed as a public input.

nodes.title: Typed samplers, deciders, and graph distributions
nodes.statement: Define finite type and edge support and its graph-distribution semantics. Define a typed sampler on the constant FieldVector question-content carrier. Define heterogeneous typed questions and answers and total dependent deciders over arbitrary fibers. Define mathematical typed-sampler downsizing and its PMF theorem. Among question/answer content fibers, only the sampler carrier is asserted finite.

Generic executable behavior is inherited only from F06A; typed executable representation and costs remain explicit F07A-DETYPING/QPBT-043 obligations.
